problem: Ten crew files exist. spec-judge and spec-attacker lack the inputs sentence and a return block; the orchestrator's model is inherit; only the implementer declares isolation; no role declares hooks, though agent frontmatter can carry hooks natively. The test-builder is a subagent on paper (maxTurns 40, acceptEdits) and a session in practice. The permission fragment denies the path the test-builder is told to write.

questions.text: Which of the four hats the constitution names become roles in this run?
questions.why: Each new role is a crew file, a dispatch template, a return schema and a place in the workflow. Each one not taken is either a kickoff rule or a workflow stage and I will write it as that.

options.value: interface-builder: writes wave-zero seams and halts on a spec–codebase contradiction instead of iterating to green
strong-worker: one retry of a red unit on a stronger tier from a clean state before a human is asked
per-unit adversary: attacks a completed unit before merge for what its checks missed
scribe: assembles the report and log entry and notices when assembly fails

questions.answer: all four: interface-builder, strong-worker, per-unit adversary, scribe

questions.text: Is the test-builder a session agent or a dispatched subagent?
questions.why: A session agent holds the ask-user tool, has no turn budget and is started by the human; a subagent gets a sealed dispatch with a run folder in it and a return schema. The file must be one or the other.

options.value: Session agent, like the spec-builder: started by the human against a frozen spec and a run folder, may ask, returns a schema'd handoff.
Subagent with a rendered dispatch naming the run folder; it cannot ask and reports unverified nodes instead.

questions.answer: (unanswered) — decided D21: session agent, on crew-problems' finding and the provider's earlier statement

questions.text: Where is a role's reach declared?
questions.why: Today frontmatter and the settings fragment are two hand-written files that contradict. One source with the other derived, or a check that the two agree, closes the hole.

options.value: Frontmatter is the source (tools, model, isolation, permissionMode, hooks); the agent allow list is generated from it; path denies and the Bash sandbox live in settings and are the only rules not derivable from a role.
Both hand-maintained, with a check that fails when a role's tools exceed the fragment or a fragment deny hits a path a role file names.

questions.text: The spec chain (spec-builder, spec-judge, spec-attacker): frozen for calibration, or brought under the crew rules?
questions.why: D4 froze them byte-for-byte; the builder was rewritten anyway. Frozen files cannot gain the inputs sentence, a return schema or a rendered dispatch.

options.value: All three follow the crew rules in this run; calibration is re-run against the rubric bench after the change.
Judge and attacker stay byte-frozen; only the builder follows the rules.
All three stay byte-frozen; D4 stands.

questions.answer: custom: spec chain left as is; builder is a session agent, judge and attacker invoked by it; v1's 18 decisions are the first builder's, editable

questions.text: Role-scoped hooks: used in this run?
questions.why: Agent frontmatter can carry its own PreToolUse/PostToolUse/Stop hooks. A worker-only test-after-edit hook or a critic that cannot write even if its tools widen can only be expressed there.

options.value: Yes: a role's own guarantees (worker check-after-edit, read-only roles' write denial) are declared in its frontmatter hooks; global hooks keep only what applies to every role.
No: global hooks only, discriminating by phase and path as today.

questions.answer: yes: role-scoped hooks in frontmatter; global hooks only for what applies to every role
